items.title: GL Q3 deep dive: Medicare claims and group health volatility weigh on margins
items.summary: Insurance holding company Globe Life (NYSE:GL) met Wall Street’s revenue expectations in Q3 2026, with sales up 6% year on year to $1.61 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $4.84 per share was 1.1% below analysts’ consensus estimates.

items.title: Globe Life Sinks 8% as Piper Sandler Downgrade Says It’s No Longer a “Predictable Safe Haven”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysGlobe Life shares fell 8% after Piper Sandler downgraded the stock to Neutral from Overweight and cut its price target to $165 from $200. Piper Sandler says Globe Life is no longer a predictable safe haven, pointing to bigger medical claims, irregular Medicare supplement claims and softer 2027 guidance.

items.title: 5 must-read analyst questions from Globe Life’s Q3 earnings call
items.summary: Globe Life’s third quarter saw solid revenue growth, yet the market responded negatively after adjusted earnings came in below analyst expectations. Management pointed to operational headwinds in its United American General Agency Division, most notably due to a process change at the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) that led to elevated claims. Additionally, the Evri group health business experienced higher-than-expected severity in claims, contributing to lower underwriting margin

items.title: Globe Life (GL) Stock Price Shrugs Off Q3 Earnings Margin Questions
items.summary: Globe Life stock barely flinched after Q3 2026 earnings, slipping about 0.7% to US$168.41 even as the insurer posted basic earnings per share of US$4.71 and net income of US$361.1m. Short-term traders see a quiet tape. Longer term investors see a different story, centred on a company with a trailing P/E of 10.9 that sits well below a peer average of 39.2 and a model valuation that suggests the shares trade at a steep discount.
